messages:
sanjay: quick FYI — saw a cluster of tail-latency spikes this morning correlated with tenant probes hitting quota cutover points. looks like our reactive borrowing is too slow for short bursts :grimacing:

eva: can you paste the logs? which pool got drained?

sanjay: paste from gateway traces: `quota_check -> deny -> retry -> probe -> borrow_request` 90% of retries failed before borrow completed. Borrow latency ~120ms, probes are 100ms bursts so they miss the window.

carla: ugh. probecause our borrow handshake requires two RPCs + leader election for shard. that is the slow part.
\nmina: alternative idea: proactive redispatch — when we detect increased probe rate for a token, preemptively move small credit slabs from regional burst pool into tenant-local reservoir for short windows. essentially optimistic borrow.

taylor: sounds promising. tradeoffs? risk of starving other tenants during misprediction. need guardrails and a quick retract path. :thinking:

sanjay: agreed. rough sketch of policy (pseudo):
```
redispatch_policy:
  window_s: 10            # short optimistic window
  max_slabs_per_tenant: 3
  trigger_rate_rps: 5     # if tenant RPS > trigger within sample
  retract_pct: 0.5        # reduce if we hit cluster-level pressure
  verify_with_probe: true
```

eva: metrics we should emit: redispatch.decisions, redispatch.retracted, redispatch.latency, redispatch.conflicts. add correlate with per-tenant tail latency.

carla: also add a safety: only allow optimistic slabs from regional burst pool, never from reserved commits. and an emergency kill-switch via control-plane flag.

ratebot: note created: #INFR-3421 — eval redispatch vs probe-hedging. assigned to @sanjay and @carla.

ops-bot: canary plan suggestion: staged rollout -> 1% tenants -> 5% -> 20% with telemetry gates (retract_rate < 0.2 and backend_tail_p95 delta < 10ms).

mina: one more thought — tie trigger to model of probe patterns (fast probes vs sustained ramp). simplest first: RPS threshold + short window.

taylor: ok action items: (1) sanjay to prototype policy + telemetry (2w) (2) carla to work on borrow IPC fast-path (3w) (3) mina to write detection rules (1w) (4) eva to own dashboards/alerts. if all green we'll canary.

sanjay: thanks. I'll post a short RFC draft tomorrow with the config schema and safety gates. ping me if you want to pair on the prototype. :thumbsup:
